record.paper_title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems
record.context_brief: Valdivia dual ball versus Plichko structure
record.original_question: Suppose the dual unit ball (B_{X*},w*) of a Banach space X is Valdivia. Must X be Plichko, meaning that X admits a countably norming Markushevich basis?

evidence.quote: It seems to be still open if X must be Plichko under this assumption, [73].
However, it is not true that X must be 1-Plichko if (BX∗, w∗) is Valdivia, [73].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a (real) Banach space with dual $X^*$, and let $B_{X^*}$ denote its closed dual unit ball equipped with the weak* topology. A compact Hausdorff space $K$ is called Valdivia if there exists a set $\Gamma$ and a homeomorphic embedding $h : K \hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}^\Gamma$ such that the set $\{x \in h(K) : \{\gamma \in \Gamma : x(\gamma) \neq 0\} \text{ is countable}\}$ is dense in $h(K)$.

A Markushevich basis of $X$ is a biorthogonal system $\{(x_\alpha, x_\alpha^*) : \alpha \in \Lambda\} \subset X \times X^*$ such that $\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{x_\alpha : \alpha \in \Lambda\} = X$ and the functionals $\{x_\alpha^* : \alpha \in \Lambda\}$ separate the points of $X$. Such a basis is called countably norming if the set
$$D = \Big\{ x^* \in X^* : \{\alpha \in \Lambda : x^*(x_\alpha) \neq 0\} \text{ is countable} \Big\}$$
is a norming subspace of $X^*$, i.e. there exists $c > 0$ with $\|x\| \le c \sup\{|x^*(x)| : x^* \in D, \|x^*\| \le 1\}$ for all $x \in X$. A Banach space is called Plichko if it admits a countably norming Markushevich basis.

Question: If $(B_{X^*}, w^*)$ is a Valdivia compact space, must $X$ be Plichko?
artifact.status_search_result: The survey on norming Markushevich bases lists this as an open problem: while it is known that $X$ need not be 1-Plichko when $(B_{X^*}, w^*)$ is Valdivia, whether $X$ must be Plichko under this assumption is still open. Recent literature on the topic (2023–2024) does not report a resolution.

status_evidence.title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: It seems to be still open if X must be Plichko under this assumption. However, it is not true that X must be 1-Plichko if (BX*, w*) is Valdivia.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of whether a Banach space with Valdivia dual ball must be Plichko is listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Banach spaces of continuous functions without norming Markushevich bases
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on existence/nonexistence of norming Markushevich bases in C(K) spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Recent related literature does not resolve the Valdivia-ball-implies-Plichko question.
